bluf: Threat posture ELEVATED — driven by EXTREME HEAT (heat index up to 111°F, warning noon–8 PM) and a significant crime surge in SE Austin (3 homicides in 3 days, robbery-homicide suspect still at large). Summer Walker at Moody Center (~7,000) and Gary Clark Jr. at Antone's (~500) create heavy evening foot traffic. Brief all staff on heat protocols and at-large suspect.

incidents.title: Robbery-Homicide — E. Riverside AutoZone (SUSPECT AT LARGE)
incidents.detail: APD released new video June 18 of suspect wanted in the fatal shooting of mechanic Jose Salgado-Amador, 28, during a robbery at the E. Riverside AutoZone parking lot. Suspect: Hispanic male, 15–20, gray hoodie, fled in a light-colored sedan. Case is Austin's 27th homicide of 2026. Suspect remains unidentified and at large. APD renewed request for public tips. Reward: up to $1,000. Suspect at large with demonstrated willingness to use lethal force during robbery. All valet, bellstand, and exterior staff should be briefed on suspect description. Report any suspicious loitering near loading dock or guest vehicle areas.

incidents.title: Double Homicide — Old Manor Road (Husband & Wife)
incidents.detail: APD found a husband and wife dead inside a home on Old Manor Road. Case is Austin's 28th homicide investigation of 2026. Investigation ongoing; no suspect identified. No direct threat to property. Domestic in nature; monitor for spillover in guest population (DV-related incidents can sometimes involve hotels as refuge locations).

incidents.title: SE Austin Homicide Cluster — 3rd Killing in 3 Days
incidents.location: Waters at Bluff Springs, 7707 S I-35 Service Road NB
incidents.detail: A woman was found dead with trauma to her body in a public area of the Waters at Bluff Springs apartment complex at approx. 1:38 PM Wednesday. Austin's 29th homicide of 2026. No suspect information. Third homicide in SE Austin in three days. Pattern of violence in the SE Austin corridor warrants heightened awareness for any staff traveling or commuting on the S. I-35 service road. No direct threat to downtown property at this time.

incidents.title: US–Iran MOU Formally Signed — Peace Deal in Effect
incidents.detail: Trump and Iranian President Pezeshkian digitally signed the 14-point MOU in English and Farsi. Key provisions: 60-day ceasefire extension (incl. Lebanon); Strait of Hormuz reopens immediately without tolls; US lifts oil/petrochemical sanctions; $300B reconstruction fund; nuclear weapons pledge reiterated. Iran stated Hormuz will not revert to pre-war conditions and fees may apply after 60 days. Positive geopolitical development. Monitor for any opportunistic domestic protest activity tied to the signing — pro- or anti-Iran factions. No credible threat to Austin property. Juneteenth week and MOU signing may draw activist presence near UT Austin campus Friday.

civil_unrest.title: Juneteenth Week — City Offices Closed Friday
civil_unrest.detail: City of Austin municipal offices, courts, libraries, and recreation centers will be CLOSED Friday, June 19 in observance of Juneteenth. Juneteenth Parade is Friday at 9:30 AM in East Austin. Road closures expected east of I-35 beginning ~8 AM Friday. Mayor Kirk Watson participated in a Pride flag-raising and proclamation June 17.

civil_unrest.title: US–Iran MOU — Protest Watch
civil_unrest.detail: Formal signing of US-Iran MOU today may generate opportunistic demonstrations. No organized protest events confirmed in Austin. Monitor social media for pop-up activity near the Capitol or UT campus. Level may increase to MODERATE Friday if signing generates significant domestic reaction.
